title: Néron lft-model existence descends through finite flat extensions
statement: Let $D\hookrightarrow D'$ be a finite faithfully flat map of Dedekind domains, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, $E'=\operatorname{Frac}(D')$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}D'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Finite means $D'$ is a finitely generated $D$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and faithfully flat has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Let $G$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type $E$-group scheme and $H\hookrightarrow G$ a smooth closed $E$-subgroup scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $G_{E'}$ has a Néron lft-model over $S'$, then $H$ has a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model over $S$. This includes $H=G$ with the identity closed immersion. A Dedekind domain here means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a domain $D$ with fraction field $E$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$, a Néron lft-model of a smooth $E$-group $V$ means a smooth separated $S$-group $\mathcal V$, with an $E$-group isomorphism $\mathcal V_E\simeq V$ [def-pc-base-change], for which restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that each affine source chart over an affine base chart has a finitely generated coordinate algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 4, printed pp.290–291 (PDF pages 296–297), Weil restriction, schematic closure and group smoothening Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: The group $H$ is of finite type: a finite affine cover of $G$ restricts to a finite cover of $H$ by spectra of quotients of finitely generated $E$-algebras. Choose the given Néron lft-model $M'$ of $G_{E'}$. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-lft-weil-restriction-geometry] to obtain $W=\operatorname{Res}_{S'/S}M'$, smooth separated commutative, with $W_E$ and $W^0$ of finite type. The adjunction gives a generic group homomorphism $a:H\to W_E$ corresponding to the inclusion $H_{E'}\hookrightarrow G_{E'}$.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, first paragraph; 7.6 Theorem 4 and Proposition 5 Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $H_{E'}\hookrightarrow G_{E'}$ is a closed immersion. The map $a$ is a monomorphism on functors of points: if two $T\to H$ have equal composites with $a$, their base changes to $T_{E'}$ have equal composites with the given closed immersion $H_{E'}\hookrightarrow G_{E'}$, hence are equal; equality descends along the faithfully flat finite cover $T_{E'}\to T$ by [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], viewing schemes as spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $a$. Its scheme-theoretic kernel is the trivial group because of this monomorphism. The factorization's quotient sheaf is therefore $H/1=H$, so its faithfully flat factor is an isomorphism and $a$ identifies $H$ with a closed finite-type subgroup of $W_E$.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, canonical generic closed immersion; expanded using the Homomorphism Theorem and fpqc equality Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text:
For a smooth $S$-scheme $X$, [lem-pc-smooth-flat] makes $X$ flat and locally finitely presented. Its base change $X'=X\times_SS'$ is smooth over $S'$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change], since $S'\to S$ is flat. Adjunction, the Néron mapping property of $M'$, and generic base-change compatibility give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(X',M')\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{E'}(X'_{E'},G_{E'})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,W_E).$$
Here $X'_{E'}=X_E\times_EE'$: localizing $D'$ at the nonzero elements of $D$ gives $E'$ because it is a finite domain over the field $E$. All three bijections send an integral morphism to its generic restriction.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, functorial Néron property of the Weil restriction; 7.6 Proposition 6 Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Let $C\hookrightarrow W$ be the schematic closure of $a(H)$ supplied by [lem-sfb-dedekind-lft-generic-subgroup-closure]. It is a flat separated commutative lft group with $C_E=a(H)\simeq H$, hence has smooth finite-type generic fibre. The ambient $W$ is smooth separated and $W^0$ is of finite type by step 1, so [lem-sfb-lft-closed-subgroup-group-smoothening] gives $u:N\to C$, with $N$ smooth separated commutative lft, $N_E\simeq H$, and unique lifting of every smooth-test-scheme map to $C$.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, flat closure and group smoothening; 7.1 Theorem 5 Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Given smooth $X/S$ and $f_E:X_E\to H$, step 3 extends $a f_E$ uniquely to $b:X\to W$. The flatness of $X$ and [lem-sfb-dedekind-lft-generic-subgroup-closure] factor $b$ uniquely through $C$; [lem-sfb-lft-closed-subgroup-group-smoothening] then lifts it uniquely to $N$. Conversely any lift has generic fibre $f_E$: its composite with the generic closed immersion $a$ agrees with $a f_E$, and $a$ is a monomorphism. Two lifts with the same generic fibre have the same composite to $W$ by step 3, then the same map to $C$ by the closed immersion, and finally coincide by the smoothening bijection. Thus restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,H)$ is bijective. The group structure and generic group isomorphism came from step 4. This proves the claimed Néron lft-model, including the identity inclusion $H=G$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-969331e37 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all three new nodes in full. The local BLR copy is absent; I checked the claims of BLR 7.1/5, 7.6/4-5 and 10.1/4 directly. The item statement is unchanged, matches BLR 10.1/4, and the parent semiabelian-lft node uses it with G=H=P. Step 1: H is finite type (elementary); the restriction node gives W, with W_E and W^0 of finite type and a generic homomorphism a. Step 2: a is a monomorphism, since equality after composing with the closed immersion (01QR node) descends along the finite faithfully flat cover T_{E'}->T by the fpqc-sheaf node. The homomorphism theorem (Milne 5.39 node; H and W_E are separated and finite type) then gives a trivial kernel, H/1=H, and a closed immersion. Step 3: smooth implies flat and lfp, and the 02V4 node gives X' smooth. The chain of adjunction, Neron property of M' and base change is correct, and D' tensor E = E'. Steps 4-5: every hypothesis of the closure node (M=W, J=a(H)) and of the smoothening node (W^0 finite type, C flat with C_E=H) holds. Existence comes from the flat-test-scheme factorization and the smoothening lift; uniqueness from injectivity in step 3, then the closed immersion, then the smoothening bijection. The generic fibre is correct because a is a monomorphism. New nodes are statement-only, self-contained and have complete stmt_deps, and all three are true. Restriction node: W is commutative by Neron uniqueness. W^0 is quasi-compact, which I checked independently with a U*U covering argument. Closure node: torsion-free over a Dedekind domain gives flat, and formation commutes with localization. Smoothening node: the BLR lft extension, with universal property for all smooth X. They are not duplicates: the existing Weil-restriction and Hom nodes give algebraic spaces only, the existing closure node is DVR and finite type, and the existing normalization and finite-cover nodes change the base and have no universal property. No restatement of the item and no cycle. Batch 5: the four flagged closures reach only general definitions and facts (def-trf-algebraic-space, def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion). None is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so no assumption leaf is needed. Accepted tool_uses: closed-immersion base change, fpqc sheaf and smooth-flat. No changes.
